title: Minimax Risk Brackets for Transported Causal Means near a Manifold Tube
banked_reason: The delivered theorem combines a radius-dependent geometric lower floor with an ambient-dimensional regression upper bound; at zero radius its source exponents remain s/(2s+k) versus (s wedge 1)/(2(s wedge 1)+d).
gap_reasons: Matching is established only where target sampling dominates the generic regression guarantee, and neither the joint-interaction term, a strict two-sample phase, nor honest interval lengths is delivered.
The EP2 inconsistency result concerns the note's own excessively sparse projection construction and does not establish a limitation of an existing broadly used method.

The zero-radius exponent already appears in Chen–Gao's public theorem text, leaving the bounded Bernoulli realization and tube-radius interpolation as a modest extension rather than a new transport characterization.
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage work derived a radius-uniform lower bound from bounded-outcome fixed-count source and target pairs, and a data-only local-ball upper bound for the same observational transport class. Its proposed empirical-projection estimator was shown inconsistent on a legal sparse-grid law, so the matched three-term frontier and honest interval claim were left open. An independent validity gate found the delivered bracket sound but below the field novelty floor; a new occupancy-aware estimator and matching source-target converse remain future research.
tldr: The delivered result is a dimension-general, radius-uniform minimax risk bracket for the transported causal mean, together with the separate EP2 estimator refutation at its original reference inputs. For arbitrary fixed legal \(d\ge2\), \(1\le m<d\), \(k=d-m\), \(0<s\le2\), legal \(\alpha\), and \(\gamma>d/2\), choose the accommodating public inputs and flat-ball graph bounds in Theorem \(\ref{thm:radius-uniform-observational-bracket}\). Writing \(q=s\wedge1\), every \(n,N\ge1\) and \(0\le\rho\le\rho_0\) satisfy \(c\max\{N^{-1/2},\min\{n^{-s/(2s+k)},(n\rho^k)^{-1/2}\}\}\le\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{obs}}_{n,N,\rho}\le C\{N^{-1/2}+n^{-q/(2q+d)}\}\). At zero radius the source lower floor is \(n^{-s/(2s+k)}\), with elbow \(\rho=n^{-1/(2s+k)}\). The upper inequality uses one explicit sample-only local-ball estimator, and the bracket matches at order \(N^{-1/2}\) when \(N\le n^{2q/(2q+d)}\). The original \(d=2\), \(s=1/8\) segment theorem remains a numerical corollary, while a separate legal fixed law makes EP2 risk tend to one. The pair term, nuisance converse, and sharp source upper rate outside the certified regime remain open.
gap: Thin-set integration assumes a known target weight, Zhang--Liu--Wang--Teng match the covariate-shift moment problem only with known source and target laws and give only an upper guarantee for their unknown-law truncation, ordinary transport theory uses full-dimensional density-ratio overlap, and higher-order causal-functional theory does not account for a target support whose effective projection count changes with scale and tube radius.
fill: The project supplies an estimable inverse-small-ball overlap condition, a total empirical-projection and U-statistic estimator with explicit singular-matrix conventions and a finite-grid public bandwidth rule, and matched upper and lower bounds exhibiting distinct thin- and thick-tube observational nuisance phases.
